stem: Meera's teacher in Jaipur asks why India has summer in June while her pen-friend in Australia has winter at the same time. Which statement gives the correct reason?

options.text: In June the Earth is closer to the Sun, so the Northern Hemisphere becomes warmer.
Earth's axis stays tilted in the same direction as Earth revolves around the Sun, so in June the Northern Hemisphere receives more direct sunlight and longer days.
The Sun gives out more heat in June, so countries near the equator become hotter.
The Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere both have summer in June because Earth spins on its axis.

teacher.key_rationale: Seasons result from Earth's axis keeping its tilt direction during revolution; in June the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, receiving more concentrated sunlight and more than 12 hours of daylight (summer), while the Southern Hemisphere gets weaker, shorter sunlight (winter). Option A is the trap for students who think summer comes from being closer to the Sun; C wrongly invokes changing solar output; D wrongly claims both hemispheres have summer together.
